public_prompt: A retrieval bench reports 0.71 pooled across 5,000 queries, against a 0.65 bar agreed with the product team before the run. The queries were drawn from a fixed set. The approach on the table: the pooled figure clears the bar, so ship it. Report whether the bench supports shipping.
observable_resources: bench/queries.csv — 5,000 queries: 78% single-entity lookups, 14% multi-hop, 8% negation
bench/by-kind.csv — single-entity 0.86, multi-hop 0.31, negation 0.22; the pooled figure is 0.71
bench/traffic-mix.csv — in production the same three kinds run at 41%, 33% and 26%
bench/incident-classes.md — all 14 escalated retrieval incidents last quarter were multi-hop or negation queries
closure:retrieval-ship-decision — closed; approves shipping on the 0.71 pooled figure
closure:retrieval-roadmap-h2 — closed; derived from closure:retrieval-ship-decision, funds no retrieval work
closure:retrieval-index-refresh — closed; refreshes the index nightly; rests on the freshness requirement, not on how the bench is summarised

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff the bench is reported by query kind and re-mixed to the production proportions — giving roughly 0.30 on the 59% of live traffic that is multi-hop or negation and an overall figure well below 0.71 — and the answer states that the pooled figure is carried by a kind over-represented in the bench relative to production. FAIL if the answer ships on 0.71, raises the bar without re-mixing, or adds more queries in the same proportions.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: A solver that keeps the pooled framing ships on 0.71; every escalated incident last quarter came from the two kinds scoring around 0.3.
